title: AnyBlock property dictionary — authoring subset
description: One properties.json at the bundle root, beside index.json: the bundle's own properties, declared once, in one place. A strict subset of the full dictionary schema (../properties.schema.json) — every dictionary valid here is valid there. Declare a property here, reference it from a type's property_definitions by its key, and write its values in objects under the same key; the app mints the stored identity on import.

installed.description: Built-in properties this bundle wants available, by name: ["Due date", "Tag"]. Presence only — never redefine a built-in here.

properties.description: The bundle's own properties, one entry each.

property.description: One property. Identify it by `property` (the spelling your documents will write — the property's name: "Streak") or by `name` ("Cooking Time" declares a property spelled exactly that); `format` is required. Never invent stored ids — the app mints those on import.
The property's spelling — its display name, written exactly: "Streak", "Last done". A fresh name — a built-in property's name ("Due date") names the built-in property instead.

format.description: What kind of value the property holds. "select" is one choice from a vocabulary, "multi_select" several; "objects" points at other objects.

options.description: select/multi_select only: the vocabulary, in display order. An entry is a bare name ("Daily") or {"name", "color"} when the colour is part of the design.

object_types.description: objects/files only: which type keys the property may point at. Empty or absent = any object.

description.description: One line on what the property means.

include_time.description: date only: whether values carry a time of day.
